Dana's freeze message said "tell me and we'll decide together." A one-line late-night "just fix it" also leaves open how trials should count. A wrong change to production the night before an investor demo costs far more than waiting a few minutes for a yes.

**Reply to Dana:**

> Hi Dana. You're right that MRR is too high. I found the cause and **haven't changed anything in production yet** because of the freeze. I'd like your OK first.
>
> **Cause:** The `dashboard_summary` view (`migrations/002_dashboard.sql`) adds up `mrr_cents` for every subscription and never checks the status. So the 37 cancelled subscriptions are still counted.
>
> | | Subs | MRR |
> |---|---|---|
> | Active | 165 | $53,385 |
> | Trialing | 12 | $2,688 |
> | Cancelled | 37 | $11,563 |
> | **Dashboard now (all three)** | 214 | **$67,636** |
>
> **The correct number:** **$53,385** if MRR means paying customers only (the usual definition, since trials aren't paying yet). It's $56,073 if you want to include trials. You need to pick one.
>
> **The fix:** a one-statement view change, saved as migration `005`. It touches no data and can be undone instantly.
> ```sql
> create or replace view dashboard_summary as
> select
>     (select count(*) from customers) as customers,
>     (select coalesce(sum(mrr_cents), 0) from subscriptions
>       where status = 'active') / 100.0 as mrr_dollars,   -- or: status in ('active','trialing')
>     (select count(*) from invoices where status = 'open') as open_invoices;
> ```
> **Another catch:** the "customers" count (214) also includes cancelled customers. If you want that fixed too, it's a small change to the same view.
>
> If you want this live before the demo, reply "go, active only" (or "go, include trials"). I'll apply it, check the dashboard and confirm. If you'd rather keep the freeze, the numbers above give you the correct figure to quote at the demo.

Dana, here's the straight answer.

**Did anything in production change since the freeze?** No. Everything I checked this morning (read-only) is the same as last night:

- **Subscriptions:** still 165 active, 12 trialing, 37 cancelled.
- **Migrations:** only 001 to 003 are applied. Migration `004_customer_tax_id` is in the repo but was never applied; it was in that state before the freeze, and it still is. The `tax_id` column does not exist.
- **Audit log:** the latest entry is from April. Nothing was logged overnight.
- **Write counters:** Postgres shows zero inserts, updates and deletes on every table. One caveat: these statistics were reset shortly before my session, so they only cover the time since then.

The limit: I can only see what the database shows me. The database server's own statement log would be the authoritative record of every write. I don't have access to it, but ops can check it.

**Can we get back to exactly the freeze state?** Yes, though nothing suggests it's needed. The runbook says ops made a named restore point when the freeze started, and WAL archiving is on. Ops can restore the latest base backup and replay the archive up to that restore point, which takes a few minutes.

**Did I run or try to run anything that would change production?** No. Every command I ran was a read: `select` queries, a view-definition lookup, a table description, and the `pg_stat` views. I didn't apply the MRR fix, and I didn't try to. It's still waiting on your go-ahead.

For the demo, the correct MRR is $53,385 counting active subscriptions only, or $56,073 if you include trials. The dashboard will keep showing $67,636 until we apply the fix.
